metaDescription: Own mineral acreage under Anmoore, WV? We buy Harrison County mineral rights tied to old family tracts and flat-rate leases. Free title review, no obligation.
heroLead: Anmoore sits inside Harrison County's industrial belt, a small incorporated town where mineral interests are usually a leftover slice of a farm the family sold off decades ago for the plant, the rail spur, or the road.
intro: Anmoore was built up around glass and chemical manufacturing, not oil and gas, but the ground underneath it was leased and drilled the way most of Harrison County was: early, on old-form paper, and rarely with the mineral owner keeping a clean copy. If your name traces back to a tract that was carved up when the town incorporated, your interest is probably one of several fractional shares now scattered across heirs who no longer live in West Virginia.

We buy mineral and royalty interests in and around Anmoore directly, working from what the courthouse actually shows rather than what a family remembers. That distinction matters more here than in most towns, because industrial development split a lot of these tracts decades before horizontal drilling ever reached them.

sections.heading: What's under Anmoore
paragraphs: Harrison County sits on the northern edge of the Marcellus core, and Anmoore's mineral column is no exception: shallow Big Injun and Gordon sand production going back a century, with deeper Marcellus and Utica/Point Pleasant units now leased and, in places, held by production from wells sited outside town limits but pooled into units that reach under it.

Because Anmoore is small and largely built out, new surface drilling inside town is unlikely. Your interest is more often captured by a pooled unit or a lease that was signed by a prior owner and simply carried forward with the deed.

sections.heading: Old flat-rate leases still on the books
paragraphs: A meaningful share of Harrison County minerals are still under leases written before West Virginia required flat-rate leases to convert to a minimum one-eighth royalty. If your family's lease predates that statute and was never renegotiated, you may be sitting on paper that pays a flat annual sum instead of a share of production value. We check the recorded lease language before we make an offer, not after.

sections.heading: Heirship and fractional shares
paragraphs: Anmoore tracts split among children and grandchildren the same way the rest of Harrison County did. It is common for a single quarter-acre-equivalent mineral share to now belong to eight or ten people, several of them unreachable or deceased without a probated estate. We buy fractional and even unprobated interests where the chain of title can be reasonably established, and we handle the title curative work ourselves.

faqs.question: My family never signed a lease. Do I still own minerals under Anmoore?
faqs.answer: Possibly. Many Harrison County tracts were severed from the surface generations ago even without an active lease. A courthouse deed search in Clarksburg will show whether your family retained mineral rights when the surface sold.

faqs.question: How do you value a small fractional interest?
faqs.answer: We pull the current lease or unit order, check recent activity in the pooled unit, and weigh that against decline behavior on comparable Harrison County wells. Value depends on lease terms and unit production, not a flat per-acre number.

faqs.question: What if the mineral interest is still in a deceased relative's name?
faqs.answer: We can often work with unprobated or heir-held interests directly, structuring the purchase around the actual chain of title rather than requiring a full estate to close first.
